document.abstract: The application of digital techniques in the broadcast studio has changed dramatically the on-air look of television in recent years. The creative possibilities realized by the digital approach seem endless as directors and producers discover almost un-imagined freedom.

authors.bio: Richard Taylor graduated from Manchester University with a Bachelor's Degree and from London University with a Master's Degree to begin his career with EMI in their Research Laboratories in the field of pattern recognition. Mr. Taylor's first contact with broadcast television was when he applied pattern recognition techniques to solving the problem of the automatic registration of color cameras. Later he moved on to design real-time digital- video processing equipment in the form of standards converters for both infrared cameras and radar systems, but eight years ago he decided to return to what had become his main interest of broadcast television and moved to Quant el Limited as Managing Director. Quant el was formed to exploit digital television techniques on behalf of the broadcaster and has developed a range of equipment that includes digital timebase correctors, digital synchronizers, digital production effects devices, digital still stores, and digital graphic art systems. In 1981, Mr. Taylor received the Montreux Gold Medal for Achievement in television engineering. In the 1982 New Year's Honours, Mr. Taylor was awarded the O.B.E. for services to Export.
